chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not derive omens from the Quran.

key_terms.تَفَأُّل: Divination or deriving omens from signs or texts

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using the Quran for divination or omens?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits istiqshah, a pre-Islamic practice of selecting random Quranic verses to predict fortune, distinguishing it from legitimate tafsir and tadabbur. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the Quran's integrity as a source of divine guidance rather than a tool for superstitious divination. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to avoid reducing the sacred text to mere omens while engaging with its deeper meanings.
